readings.reading_text:
[RS; reported unknown]
External research conversation example; unverified and not a professional method. Do not assume this example happened to the current user or copy promises or self-disclosures.
seeker: I am very depressed

supporter: Hello there, how are you doing?

seeker: I feel lonely

supporter: I'm sorry to hear you're feeling depressed and lonely. Is there any reason in particular you're feeling this way?

seeker: I felt go to death

supporter: You feel as though you want to die?
supporter: What is causing you to feel this way?

supporter: Did something happen at home, work, or in your personal life?
seeker: Yes. I want to die. because I love him. But he leave me alone

seeker: I think I did not able to  return my normal life

supporter: Losing a loved is very hard. 
seeker: Yes. I feel very sad. Give me some counselling
supporter: Do you have anyone you can talk to about your feelings and concerns?
seeker: I did not have close friends

supporter: My understanding is that you have lost a loved one and that is causing you to feel depressed, correct?
seeker: Yes

supporter: Do you have any family members you can speak to?
seeker: My parents. But they are avoiding me because this lover is hurting my parents also. So they are advising me many times

seeker: But I did not hear their advice

supporter: It sounds like you are going through a very rough time.
seeker: So they are angry with me.

seeker: Yes. I am very depressed. Do you give me any counselling?

supporter: I think it may be helpful to reach out to your parents to open a line of communication and discuss your differences
seeker: I will try many times. But they are avoiding me.

supporter: That must be very difficult not having your parents to support you and your loved one. 
supporter: Do you ahve any siblings?
seeker: Yes. They are did not understanding my current situation
supporter: have you tried communicating your side of the story?
seeker: Yes. I have one brother. But he was very little boy. So he did not understand my feelings.

supporter: It sounds as though your family does not agree with or understand your situation.
seeker: Yes. I try to tell my parents many times

seeker: My parents are angry with me.

supporter: Do you have anyone else in your life you are close to, I know you said you don't have any close friends.
seeker: Yes . Only one friend

seeker: But she was long distance to me

seeker: So very difficult to contact 

supporter: Would you feel comfortable talking to her about how you are feeling now?
seeker: Yes

supporter: Maybe you could text, call. or email her. It sounds like she would know better whats going on in your personal life.
seeker: I will tell my problem already in Email. But she doesn't replay to me.

supporter: That must feel terrible, I'm sorry you're having a hard time. I would feel the same way in your situation.
seeker: I try to call her but did not reached
supporter: Do you have any hobbies or interests?
seeker: Yes. I am very interested to reading comic books

seeker: I love comic books and story books

supporter: I love comic books too! Do you have any favorites?
seeker: Yes.

supporter: When you're reading comics or engaging in other hobbies does it make you feel any better?
seeker: Saga this is my favorite comic book

seeker: I will try

seeker: Very thanks for your idea

supporter: My suggestion would be when you start feeling down, take some deep breaths, go for a walk, and engage in one of your hobbies.
seeker: Ok. Very thanks.

seeker: I am very relax this times

supporter: You're welcome.
supporter: I'm glad youre feeling a little bit better.
seeker: I feel like the burden on my mined has gone down
seeker: Yes. I feel little bit better

supporter: I'm glad to hear it!
seeker: Thank you my friend
seeker: Can you tell me your name please?

supporter: Is there anything else i can do for you?
supporter: My name is Ryan. what is your name?
seeker: Riya

supporter: Its been a pleasure speaking to you riya
seeker: Thank you Ryan brother

supporter: is there anything else I can help you with today?
supporter: You're welcome Riya. I hope you take my advice moving forward and things improve for you.
seeker: Ok thank you so much for your tips

seeker: Bye

supporter: you are welcome, take care
seeker: Take care. Bye.

readings.head: MS
readings.reading_text:
[MS; reported 2024-03-12]
Complete past session (original utterances; not verified world facts):
supporter: Hey Kelly, how are you doing today?
seeker: Hey, to be honest, I'm struggling a bit.
supporter: I'm here to listen. Do you want to share what's been challenging for you?
seeker: It's my thesis. I had a setback recently, and it's just really bringing me down.
supporter: I can imagine that must be tough. What happened with your thesis?
seeker: I got some feedback that I wasn't expecting. It made me realize there's a lot more work to do than I thought.
supporter: That sounds overwhelming. It can be really hard to digest unexpected feedback.
seeker: Exactly. I was feeling quite confident before, and now I just feel lost.
supporter: It's okay to feel that way. Remember, feedback is part of the process. How are you managing these feelings?
seeker: Not too well, honestly. I've been pretty demotivated and haven't been able to get much done.
supporter: It's understandable to feel stuck. Sometimes taking a step back can help. Have you tried taking a break from it all?
seeker: I've tried, but it's hard not to think about it. It feels like I'm letting myself down.
supporter: You're not letting yourself down. You're doing your best under challenging circumstances. Remember when your friend mentioned overcoming similar doubts in his studies?
seeker: Oh yeah, he struggled with something similar and he got through it. It took him a bit of time though.
supporter: Exactly. Maybe his story can be a reminder that it's possible to bounce back. Have you reached out to your friends recently?
seeker: Not recently. Maybe I should. Talking to someone who understands might help.
supporter: That sounds like a great idea. And remember, I'm always here for you too. You have support.
seeker: Thanks, I really appreciate that. It does help to know I'm not alone in this.
supporter: You definitely aren't alone. How about focusing on one small step you can take today?
seeker: Maybe I can start by reviewing the feedback more calmly, with a fresh perspective.
supporter: That sounds like a constructive plan. Taking it step by step and being kind to yourself on the journey can make a big difference.
seeker: I’ll try to keep that in mind. Thank you for listening and helping me process things.
supporter: Anytime, Kelly. You’ve got this, even if it doesn’t feel like it right now. Keep reaching out, okay?
seeker: I will. Thanks again.

supporter: I'm here to listen. Do you want to share what's been challenging for you?
seeker: It's my thesis. I had a setback recently, and it's just really bringing me down.
supporter: I can imagine that must be tough. What happened with your thesis?
seeker: I got some feedback that I wasn't expecting. It made me realize there's a lot more work to do than I thought.
supporter: That sounds overwhelming. It can be really hard to digest unexpected feedback.
seeker: Exactly. I was feeling quite confident before, and now I just feel lost.
supporter: It's okay to feel that way. Remember, feedback is part of the process. How are you managing these feelings?
seeker: Not too well, honestly. I've been pretty demotivated and haven't been able to get much done.
supporter: It's understandable to feel stuck. Sometimes taking a step back can help. Have you tried taking a break from it all?

seeker: Not recently. Maybe I should. Talking to someone who understands might help.
supporter: That sounds like a great idea. And remember, I'm always here for you too. You have support.
seeker: Thanks, I really appreciate that. It does help to know I'm not alone in this.

seeker: Maybe I can start by reviewing the feedback more calmly, with a fresh perspective.
supporter: That sounds like a constructive plan. Taking it step by step and being kind to yourself on the journey can make a big difference.
seeker: I’ll try to keep that in mind. Thank you for listening and helping me process things.

seeker: Well, I could move out but I can't afford to rent a flat on my own. I'd have to move in with my parents, realistically.

supporter: are your parents supportive of that idea?

supporter: my guess is he felt the same way you are feeling right now
seeker: Yes. It is just such a deep betrayal. I think I could have forgiven him if it had just been a one time mistake but he had been seeing her for ages. 
supporter: watch the brene brown video on youtube with the cartoon animal about empathy - it should help when looking for friends to rely upon
supporter: grrrr. that would make me angry too
seeker: It is nice to have things to distract myself from the things that are making me feel terrible. Do you have any other suggestions for distractions? 
seeker: I just keep thinking that every evening when he was returning home with me and with every nice thing he said he was being false. 
supporter: i'm totally into the podcasts "a slob comes clean" basically it's about getting your poop in a group
seeker: Hmm that sounds .. interesting :D. Is that a metaphor? 
supporter: that's so hard. imagine how much energy he had to use to keep his lives from colliding. he couldn't find a better use for that energy?!
seeker: I know, right!! Do you think it would be helpful for me to try and talk to this woman and see how she feels? I dunno if she even realises that he was in a committed relationship 
supporter: yes! LOL but it's been helping me focus my anxiety into being a bit more productive
seeker: Anything that will help me with my anxiety is worth trying at the moment. 
supporter: what do you want to hear from her? is there anything she could say that woudl make you feel better?
supporter: NO!! she's not going to be able to help you unless you need a witness for divorce court
seeker: It would be less of a betrayal, I think, if she did not know about me. I would never do that to another woman! 
supporter: she likely knew, othewise how would he explain all the time he spent with you to her?
seeker: I suppose that's a good point too. I think maybe I do just need to make a total break and not look back. 
seeker: I do appreciate you talking, you have helped me to see things a great deal more clearly than I previously did.
supporter: glad i could help. please stay safe and no matter what you decide to do, you will be fine.
seeker: Thank you and the same to you! Have a nice rest of day.

seeker: Hey, thanks for being here. I just need to talk a bit.
supporter: Of course, Linda. What's on your mind?
seeker: I've been trying to keep up with everything, but it's just a lot. Work, wedding plans, and now I've added meditation into the mix to help with stress.
supporter: It sounds like you have a lot on your plate. How is the meditation going so far?
seeker: It's been interesting. Some days it helps, and other days it's hard to focus. I keep thinking about the next thing I need to do.
supporter: That's understandable. It's hard to quiet the mind when so much is happening. Have you noticed any particular moments when stress hits the hardest?
seeker: Usually when I'm at home trying to relax, ironically. David is supportive, but I feel guilty about how much I'm depending on him.
supporter: Leaning on someone you love isn't a bad thing, Linda. Have you talked to David about how you're feeling?
seeker: Not in depth. I think I'm scared he'll think I'm not ready for the commitment if I show too much of my stress.
supporter: It's important to let him in on your struggles. He might surprise you with how understanding he is. Plus, it might ease some of your stress sharing it with him.
seeker: You're right. I suppose I've always been the type to handle things on my own, even when I was arguing with Lily. But, it's exhausting.
supporter: You've come a long way since then, reestablishing your bond with Lily and even adopting Buddy for emotional support. It's okay to embrace new support systems.
seeker: Buddy has been a joy, definitely helps lift my spirits on rough days. I forgot how much a pet can change the atmosphere.
supporter: Pets have a special way of comforting us. It's like they know when we need a little extra love. How's Buddy adjusting?
seeker: He's a bundle of energy and keeps me distracted in a good way. Sometimes, I wish I could have his carefree attitude.
supporter: Sounds like Buddy is a wonderful addition. And taking things one moment at a time, like he does, might help. How has your health been since the doctor's visit?
seeker: The meditation is helping, slowly. My doctor suggested regular breaks from wedding planning and work emails to keep things in balance.
supporter: That sounds like solid advice. Creating boundaries can be really beneficial. Would David be able to help with some of the planning?
seeker: I think he would. I've been hesitant to delegate, but maybe it's time to ease my load a bit.
supporter: Letting go of some of the responsibilities can relieve a lot of pressure. You're already doing so much just by working on your mental health.
seeker: Thank you. I guess I needed a reminder that it's okay to ask for help and not do everything alone.
supporter: Exactly. You're doing your best and that's all anyone can ask. Remember, you're not alone in this.
seeker: Thanks for talking this through with me. I feel a little lighter knowing I have support.
supporter: Anytime, Linda. Just keep breathing and reaching out whenever you need someone to listen.

seeker: Hello I am here to discuss my anxiety over the current pandemic. 

supporter: Hey there! That's a good topic to talk about. With everything that's been going on, it's normal to feel some anxiety.
supporter: What do you think is one thing that is giving you a lot of anxiety?
seeker: Thank you very much for your understanding. Yeah it's tough especially with rising cases for the past two weeks or so in my city. 
seeker: I live in Canada and my city is pretty good so far and really low on numbers but have been seeing new cases every day for the last two weeks or so

seeker: so that adds anxiety to me when I go out and I am more on guard and paranoid 

supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Similar stuff is happening where I am, and I also get anxious hearing about it.
seeker: And we had a lock-down earlier this year and yet, with the exception of one province, every province remains operational at full speed despite lock-downs earlier, and now a lot of provinces are seeing record cases with the second wave.

seeker: yeah I hope you get through this okay also and stay safe and well.

supporter: What do you feel when you feel on guard and paranoid? Try to say some more about that if you can.
supporter: Thanks, I hope the same for you.
seeker: I go out pretty much only when I have a purpose and personal admin/errands. I work about one or two days a week out of my home. So with the rising cases, I just feel anxious having to get out of the safety of my home. I was a lot more anxious earlier this year though. I am much more used to it at this time. 

seeker: And it's hard where everyday is the same for me and staying at home, without a change of pace like even simple walks outside, going to the gym, or going to hike or run etc. I pretty much missed out the whole year after March. My life has been on hold and I am just surprised that it's even november now, because it feels like I am still stuck in March. 

supporter: Yeah, that makes sense. When this was all new, the uncertainty probably made for more anxiety. Now that we know some more about what is safe and what isn't, maybe less so.

But it doesn't mean the anxiety is gone, of course. It's still around in our day-to-day lives.
supporter: Well said. You feel stuck. The usual things you would do now are just not available to you.
seeker: yeah I have been adjusting to it and the cases were down and even to zero in my city for most of the last few months, but there's definitely the start of a new community spread now. 


seeker: yes correct

seeker: Plus there's a loss of routine or motivation. I procrastinate a lot and get lost in thought or lost without thought. I don't work out as much as I used to (inside or outside of home). I don't eat as well and my sleep pattern is not good at all (I sleep a lot later than I should). 

seeker: So I am disappointed in myself to say the least.

seeker: and also feeling guilty to see myself waste my life and time this way and not being productive

supporter: I can rephrase some of this, if you don't mind. In a way, you're talking about activities that you may have used (gym, hikes, etc) to keep yourself in a good mood. Now that those don't seem available, you just don't have those opportunities to boost your mood. It makes sense that you would be feeling this way.
seeker: now I am more used to it of course, but this summarizes how I have been feeling for most of this year. 

supporter: I think you explained yourself really well. Thanks for sharing how you've been feeling.
seeker: yes you're right. That's exactly it. I think it's going to be this way for a long time. I see other people compromising and taking the risk to go out for walks or runs, and even to the gym. I could have done that for the last few months when we had zero cases for awhile, but I didn't want to gamble and compromise. And I still see those people as selfish when I choose to do what I think is right. 

seeker: yeah no worries. It's good that you understand and thank you for listening. 

supporter: Do you think if you went ahead anyway to the gym or out for runs that you would feel guilty for doing them?
seeker: We won't know more about the mental implications and the sociological aspects of the pandemic probably until years to come. 

seeker: I thought about that

supporter: Yeah, and that just throws on another layer of why things are difficult right now. No one wants to feel guilty for doing things that could help themselves.
seeker: to the gym, I certainly would. Because it's indoors and I do feel it's unsafe as there are many equipment that others could touch. Running I felt that way because the path that I usually run on is narrow and other people walk through it also. However, I did have second thoughts about that when the case numbers were down. But I finally decided to keep doing it and stick to all outdoor trips for essential business. 


seeker: but that's just me, and I know we all have different personalities, preferences, and tolerances of risks and acceptances, etc.

supporter: Have you ever heard of the phrase "black or white thinking?" As in, thinking that situations or people are completely good or completely bad? Or completely doable or completely impossible?
seeker: so in my opinion, I feel a little indignant at the people that have been going out frivolously like there's nothing going on, to even gamble their safety and their family's. Like I live in an apartment building, and the people around me and below me are always going out, even for the last few months. So I don't feel safe either but also indignant that others are doing what I could have done, but that I had compromised on for my safety and everyone else's safety. So I just didn't feel it was fair for them to do that when I could have done that anytime I wanted. 

seeker: black and white thinking...let me think 

seeker: for this pandemic, it's pretty much black and white

supporter: Yeah, I think I understand that too. I get really frustrated hearing about people hosting big parties or not wearing masks because they think it's no big deal. They're putting others at risk.
seeker: Because I either go out or I don't. I have to compromise my values and everything I worked hard to preserve for the last few months to go out, even if I put on extra protection etc. And I just rigidly refuse to compromise my values because I don't believe it's right. Because if I had done that, I would have done that already, and long ago. And even though it's really hard on me.


seeker: yeah exactly. Because people are being selfish and are subjecting others to risks even if they don't care about themselves. 

seeker: but I know I am pretty extreme in my thinking. 

seeker: I really love the outdoors and I go out pretty often before the pandemic. 

seeker: But it's just that my own thinking is rigid and made up about it. 

seeker: But anyhow, that's the situation in a nutshell. 

supporter: I think we all do black-or-white thinking to some extent. We're wired to try and make sense of the world, and maybe our brains don't like to spend time on nuance and grey areas. We all tend to quickly categorize things into good or bad, easy or hard, black or white.
seeker: yeah I understand your thinking with the grey areas as well. I suppose for this case, it's all black and white for me, no grea areas or compromises.

seeker: that's good analysis by the way.

seeker: But anyhow I am good to go then. Thank you so very much for understanding and for your valuable inputs. 

supporter: Does this time have to be a "waste" for you? With no productivity? That seems pretty extreme.
seeker: it's a fascinating area though, fascinating thinking. I am also curious on the social and mental implications of this in the long-run

seeker: but only time will tell

seeker: there will be so much research and books written about our times. 

seeker: well I do a lot of "waste" at home. So I am quite sluggish and lazy and lost at home. 

supporter: Thanks for saying that! I liked talking with you, and we can wrap this up. I guess I'm saying you sound thoughtful and intelligent, I'm confident that you could find ways to get more out of this time if that's what you're wanting to do.
seeker: I am productive but not as driven or productive as before at home.

seeker: for sure yeah. I am sure we can get through all this in one piece eventually.

seeker: I was thinking this also that even though this is a very tough time, we will look back on this about years from now, and say wow, we got through all that!

supporter: Not as productive? Of course! It's a pandemic. We all are.  :)    Hope you're not too hard on yourself right now.
seeker: no no I am okay thanks for asking

seeker: I am just kind of spelling in out the details of my thinking and how my life has been so far

seeker: I am actually okay
 so no worries
supporter: Ha, exactly. Maybe we're not all thriving and getting rich and adding 15 pounds of muscle during this time. But we can get through it.
seeker: yup. Exactly. Lost time can always be made up later. 

seeker: okay then. I am good to go. Thanks again and thank you for your input. It does help to just kind of vent in a way. 

supporter: Before we quit, would you want to say one specific thing you know you can do today to help yourself out?
seeker: Yeah for sure

seeker: I worked out a little bit before I started the chat. I am also doing some online courses on my own time. So I will keep working hard on those. And I hope to get back more into the routine of working out. I really do think it helps my mood if I just make more time and motivation for that.

seeker: And you seem intelligent and analytical also and you know what I mean. So I do appreciate your time and input

supporter: Nice! Good job with those things.
seeker: thanks. I hope you best of luck then with all your endeavours. I know we can all get through this time. Thank you. 

seeker: stay well and stay safe my friend

supporter: Right on, same to you. It's okay to feel anxious right now. It's okay to feel unproductive right now. It's also okay to keep on doing the things that make you feel okay. Great job keeping up the workouts and the classes.
seeker: Thank you and all the best. 

supporter: Stay well and safe to you too! Take care.

supporter: Have you ever heard of the phrase "black or white thinking?" As in, thinking that situations or people are completely good or completely bad? Or completely doable or completely impossible?
seeker: so in my opinion, I feel a little indignant at the people that have been going out frivolously like there's nothing going on, to even gamble their safety and their family's. Like I live in an apartment building, and the people around me and below me are always going out, even for the last few months. So I don't feel safe either but also indignant that others are doing what I could have done, but that I had compromised on for my safety and everyone else's safety. So I just didn't feel it was fair for them to do that when I could have done that anytime I wanted. 

seeker: black and white thinking...let me think 

seeker: for this pandemic, it's pretty much black and white

supporter: Yeah, I think I understand that too. I get really frustrated hearing about people hosting big parties or not wearing masks because they think it's no big deal. They're putting others at risk.
seeker: Because I either go out or I don't. I have to compromise my values and everything I worked hard to preserve for the last few months to go out, even if I put on extra protection etc. And I just rigidly refuse to compromise my values because I don't believe it's right. Because if I had done that, I would have done that already, and long ago. And even though it's really hard on me.


seeker: yeah exactly. Because people are being selfish and are subjecting others to risks even if they don't care about themselves. 

seeker: but I know I am pretty extreme in my thinking. 

seeker: I really love the outdoors and I go out pretty often before the pandemic. 

seeker: But it's just that my own thinking is rigid and made up about it. 

seeker: But anyhow, that's the situation in a nutshell. 

supporter: I think we all do black-or-white thinking to some extent. We're wired to try and make sense of the world, and maybe our brains don't like to spend time on nuance and grey areas. We all tend to quickly categorize things into good or bad, easy or hard, black or white.
seeker: yeah I understand your thinking with the grey areas as well. I suppose for this case, it's all black and white for me, no grea areas or compromises.

seeker: that's good analysis by the way.

seeker: But anyhow I am good to go then. Thank you so very much for understanding and for your valuable inputs. 

supporter: Does this time have to be a "waste" for you? With no productivity? That seems pretty extreme.
seeker: it's a fascinating area though, fascinating thinking. I am also curious on the social and mental implications of this in the long-run

seeker: but only time will tell

seeker: there will be so much research and books written about our times. 

seeker: well I do a lot of "waste" at home. So I am quite sluggish and lazy and lost at home. 

supporter: Thanks for saying that! I liked talking with you, and we can wrap this up. I guess I'm saying you sound thoughtful and intelligent, I'm confident that you could find ways to get more out of this time if that's what you're wanting to do.
seeker: I am productive but not as driven or productive as before at home.

seeker: for sure yeah. I am sure we can get through all this in one piece eventually.

seeker: I was thinking this also that even though this is a very tough time, we will look back on this about years from now, and say wow, we got through all that!

supporter: Not as productive? Of course! It's a pandemic. We all are.  :)    Hope you're not too hard on yourself right now.
seeker: no no I am okay thanks for asking

seeker: I am just kind of spelling in out the details of my thinking and how my life has been so far

seeker: I am actually okay
 so no worries
supporter: Ha, exactly. Maybe we're not all thriving and getting rich and adding 15 pounds of muscle during this time. But we can get through it.
seeker: yup. Exactly. Lost time can always be made up later. 

seeker: okay then. I am good to go. Thanks again and thank you for your input. It does help to just kind of vent in a way. 

supporter: Before we quit, would you want to say one specific thing you know you can do today to help yourself out?
seeker: Yeah for sure

seeker: I worked out a little bit before I started the chat. I am also doing some online courses on my own time. So I will keep working hard on those. And I hope to get back more into the routine of working out. I really do think it helps my mood if I just make more time and motivation for that.

seeker: And you seem intelligent and analytical also and you know what I mean. So I do appreciate your time and input

supporter: Nice! Good job with those things.
seeker: thanks. I hope you best of luck then with all your endeavours. I know we can all get through this time. Thank you. 

seeker: stay well and stay safe my friend

supporter: Right on, same to you. It's okay to feel anxious right now. It's okay to feel unproductive right now. It's also okay to keep on doing the things that make you feel okay. Great job keeping up the workouts and the classes.
seeker: Thank you and all the best. 

supporter: Stay well and safe to you too! Take care.

readings.reading_text:
[MS; reported 2024-08-05]
Complete past session (original utterances; not verified world facts):
supporter: Hey Jimmy, it's good to hear from you. How's everything on your end?
seeker: Hey, not too great to be honest. I tried opening up to my friends at the gathering I hosted, but it didn't go as I hoped.
supporter: I'm sorry to hear that, Jimmy. It sounds frustrating. Do you want to talk more about what happened?
seeker: Yeah, I felt like I was finally ready to share some personal stuff, and it seemed like nobody wanted to listen or take it seriously.
supporter: That must have been really tough, especially when you were putting yourself out there. How did you end up feeling after that?
seeker: I felt pretty down. It was like my feelings didn't matter to them, and it made me question if they really care about me.
supporter: It's completely understandable to feel that way. It sounds like you were looking for some support from your friends.
seeker: Exactly. I just wanted someone to hear me out and maybe offer some advice or comfort.
supporter: Feeling dismissed by friends could be really disheartening. Have you experienced anything like this before with them?
seeker: Not really. That's why it was kind of a shock. I just didn't expect it from them.
supporter: That makes it even harder when it's unexpected. Was there anyone at the gathering who you felt did listen or understand?
seeker: I think one of my friends was trying, but got caught up in someone else’s conversation. It wasn’t like they ignored me on purpose.
supporter: It sounds like they had a lot going on at the time. But still, it's important that they realize how that affected you.
seeker: Yeah, I hope I can talk to them about how I felt. I'm just not sure how to bring it up without making it awkward.
supporter: It's definitely a delicate subject, but expressing how you feel is also important. Maybe you could start by mentioning how much their support means to you?
seeker: That's a good idea. I guess I could tell them that it would really mean a lot to me if they could be there for me when I need it.
supporter: That sounds like a thoughtful way to start the conversation. Remember, real friends will want to support you when they know something's up.
seeker: Thanks, I really appreciate that. It helps to talk it through and feel a bit more prepared.
supporter: Anytime, Jimmy. I'm here for you if you need to chat more. You're doing great by taking the steps to communicate how you feel.
seeker: Thanks, it means a lot. I'll let you know how it goes.

readings.head: RS
readings.reading_text:
[RS; reported unknown]
External research conversation example; unverified and not a professional method. Do not assume this example happened to the current user or copy promises or self-disclosures.
supporter: Hello! How are you tonight?

seeker: hanging in there, kinda freaking out a little

supporter: I'm sorry to hear you are freaking out. Perhaps a friendly listening ear can encourage you?
supporter: Why are you freaking out?
seeker: I think that'll help, yeah

supporter: Sometimes just a friend to hear you out and encourage you can really make a difference. Life has its ups and down. 
seeker: I decided to leave my husband, he keeps snapping at me and won't listen to me or let me do anything
supporter: That's a difficult decision you have made. 
seeker: I'm worried how it'll go though because we have kids
supporter: Have you tried to talk to him about the problem? Or a counselor? 
seeker: I've tried to talk to him about the control issues, but he doesn't listen. He doesn't know I'm planning to leave and I think he'll try to stop me
supporter: I have worked at a domestic violence shelter before, the most dangerous time to leave a situation like this is when you leave.  Do you have a plan in place?
seeker: I have some leads on apartments and some savings I'm putting aside, and a friend I plan on living with
supporter: My husband used to be very controlling as well, I dragged him to counseling. He changed. He bucked at first, but eventually he went. We have gone a few times off and on over 20 years. We both came from broken homes.  

seeker: I haven't got 100% of the details worked out yet, but I'm trying
supporter: Has he hurt you physically? or is he mainly emotionally abusive? 

seeker: He hasn't hurt me physically
seeker: I often feel like he would but I'm also a child abuse survivor so it's hard to tell if that's true or just a memory
supporter: I'm glad to hear that. I can understand that you would be really stressed at this time, however, I do encourage you to get a good plan in place, and definitely get counseling. 
seeker: I think that's the best idea
supporter: Yes, I had child abuse in my life too, I really think counseling saved our marriage, 3 times. But like, I said, he didn't want to go. However, the first time, I did leave and stay with a friend, and that convinced him I was serious. 
seeker: that's a good thought, I wonder what he'd do if I stayed with a friend
supporter: I wish I could fix this, but I can't. The road will be rocky and I don't know how I would have made it without people to encourage and support me, so I'm glad a friend is willing to have you stay with them until you can get on your feet. 
seeker: hey may not realize I'd leave at all
seeker: me too, that's making all the difference
supporter: My husband really loved me, but coming from a broken home, he lost his mom when he was 12, so he thought controlling me was the solution, very messed up, but he had to learn to see that. 
seeker: definitely that makes sense
supporter: He feared I would die or leave him or something, but once he saw that, and realized what he was doing was hurting me and making me want to leave, he changed. But honestly, I have never understood men and why they dont' see life the way we do. Sometimes it takes that objective person to help them see it. 
seeker: I'm not convinced mine loves me, looking back it's beginning to seem like he was draining me for my income and labor
supporter: Ouch! That sounds painful to look at. 
seeker: it is, I think I was super wrong about him and overlooked red flags
supporter: People who truly love others become willing to change. Sometimes it takes a DRASTIC measure to wake them up, like leaving. He has not heard you, so many he will "hear" it when you leave. But please be careful and have a plan. 
supporter: How long have you been married?
seeker: eight years, together for 11
supporter: That's a long time. I will say a prayer for your safety and for you to get some help, hopefully he will join you. Marriage is a lot of work, but it can't be one person, it has to be two. 
supporter: Don't leave anything in writing around until after you leave. 
seeker: absolutely!
seeker: definitely no paper trail, for sure
supporter: I believe in the power of prayer too. The Serenity prayer is a good one to help me let go of my fears and do what I can, leaving the rest to God. 
seeker: I know that one, it's helping me a lot too
supporter: If I worry and get upset, then I waste energy, I have had to learn to get distracted if I find myself on that worry train, call a friend, go for a walk, just not obsess, it goes nowhere. 
supporter: And I urge you to get a counselor. 
seeker: that's good advice!
seeker: I will
seeker: Thank you
supporter: You are welcome. Watch your thinking, when it goes off track, take charge, change your thinking, get up and move about and do something else because it's not healthy for you to worry. As you said, you freak out, and that is not good for you or your children. 

seeker: definitely, I think I can do that! I feel a lot better!
supporter: It's a rough situation, it will be difficult, you seem very intelligent, have thought about this, are working on a plan and are able to discuss it. That's a big plus on yoru side. 
seeker: Thank you! I'm feeling a lot more confident!
supporter: I'm glad to hear it. Keep the faith, all will be well in due time! Sometimes rough roads really work out, but it never FEELS that way!  You have a good night! :D

seeker: Hello I am here to discuss my anxiety over the current pandemic. 

supporter: Hey there! That's a good topic to talk about. With everything that's been going on, it's normal to feel some anxiety.
supporter: What do you think is one thing that is giving you a lot of anxiety?
seeker: Thank you very much for your understanding. Yeah it's tough especially with rising cases for the past two weeks or so in my city. 
seeker: I live in Canada and my city is pretty good so far and really low on numbers but have been seeing new cases every day for the last two weeks or so

seeker: so that adds anxiety to me when I go out and I am more on guard and paranoid 

supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Similar stuff is happening where I am, and I also get anxious hearing about it.
seeker: And we had a lock-down earlier this year and yet, with the exception of one province, every province remains operational at full speed despite lock-downs earlier, and now a lot of provinces are seeing record cases with the second wave.

seeker: yeah I hope you get through this okay also and stay safe and well.

supporter: What do you feel when you feel on guard and paranoid? Try to say some more about that if you can.
supporter: Thanks, I hope the same for you.
seeker: I go out pretty much only when I have a purpose and personal admin/errands. I work about one or two days a week out of my home. So with the rising cases, I just feel anxious having to get out of the safety of my home. I was a lot more anxious earlier this year though. I am much more used to it at this time. 

seeker: And it's hard where everyday is the same for me and staying at home, without a change of pace like even simple walks outside, going to the gym, or going to hike or run etc. I pretty much missed out the whole year after March. My life has been on hold and I am just surprised that it's even november now, because it feels like I am still stuck in March. 

supporter: Yeah, that makes sense. When this was all new, the uncertainty probably made for more anxiety. Now that we know some more about what is safe and what isn't, maybe less so.

But it doesn't mean the anxiety is gone, of course. It's still around in our day-to-day lives.
supporter: Well said. You feel stuck. The usual things you would do now are just not available to you.
seeker: yeah I have been adjusting to it and the cases were down and even to zero in my city for most of the last few months, but there's definitely the start of a new community spread now. 


seeker: yes correct

seeker: Plus there's a loss of routine or motivation. I procrastinate a lot and get lost in thought or lost without thought. I don't work out as much as I used to (inside or outside of home). I don't eat as well and my sleep pattern is not good at all (I sleep a lot later than I should). 

seeker: So I am disappointed in myself to say the least.

seeker: and also feeling guilty to see myself waste my life and time this way and not being productive

supporter: I can rephrase some of this, if you don't mind. In a way, you're talking about activities that you may have used (gym, hikes, etc) to keep yourself in a good mood. Now that those don't seem available, you just don't have those opportunities to boost your mood. It makes sense that you would be feeling this way.
seeker: now I am more used to it of course, but this summarizes how I have been feeling for most of this year. 

supporter: I think you explained yourself really well. Thanks for sharing how you've been feeling.
seeker: yes you're right. That's exactly it. I think it's going to be this way for a long time. I see other people compromising and taking the risk to go out for walks or runs, and even to the gym. I could have done that for the last few months when we had zero cases for awhile, but I didn't want to gamble and compromise. And I still see those people as selfish when I choose to do what I think is right. 

seeker: yeah no worries. It's good that you understand and thank you for listening. 

supporter: Do you think if you went ahead anyway to the gym or out for runs that you would feel guilty for doing them?
seeker: We won't know more about the mental implications and the sociological aspects of the pandemic probably until years to come. 

seeker: I thought about that

supporter: Yeah, and that just throws on another layer of why things are difficult right now. No one wants to feel guilty for doing things that could help themselves.
seeker: to the gym, I certainly would. Because it's indoors and I do feel it's unsafe as there are many equipment that others could touch. Running I felt that way because the path that I usually run on is narrow and other people walk through it also. However, I did have second thoughts about that when the case numbers were down. But I finally decided to keep doing it and stick to all outdoor trips for essential business. 


seeker: but that's just me, and I know we all have different personalities, preferences, and tolerances of risks and acceptances, etc.

supporter: Have you ever heard of the phrase "black or white thinking?" As in, thinking that situations or people are completely good or completely bad? Or completely doable or completely impossible?
seeker: so in my opinion, I feel a little indignant at the people that have been going out frivolously like there's nothing going on, to even gamble their safety and their family's. Like I live in an apartment building, and the people around me and below me are always going out, even for the last few months. So I don't feel safe either but also indignant that others are doing what I could have done, but that I had compromised on for my safety and everyone else's safety. So I just didn't feel it was fair for them to do that when I could have done that anytime I wanted. 

seeker: black and white thinking...let me think 

seeker: for this pandemic, it's pretty much black and white

supporter: Yeah, I think I understand that too. I get really frustrated hearing about people hosting big parties or not wearing masks because they think it's no big deal. They're putting others at risk.
seeker: Because I either go out or I don't. I have to compromise my values and everything I worked hard to preserve for the last few months to go out, even if I put on extra protection etc. And I just rigidly refuse to compromise my values because I don't believe it's right. Because if I had done that, I would have done that already, and long ago. And even though it's really hard on me.


seeker: yeah exactly. Because people are being selfish and are subjecting others to risks even if they don't care about themselves. 

seeker: but I know I am pretty extreme in my thinking. 

seeker: I really love the outdoors and I go out pretty often before the pandemic. 

seeker: But it's just that my own thinking is rigid and made up about it. 

seeker: But anyhow, that's the situation in a nutshell. 

supporter: I think we all do black-or-white thinking to some extent. We're wired to try and make sense of the world, and maybe our brains don't like to spend time on nuance and grey areas. We all tend to quickly categorize things into good or bad, easy or hard, black or white.
seeker: yeah I understand your thinking with the grey areas as well. I suppose for this case, it's all black and white for me, no grea areas or compromises.

seeker: that's good analysis by the way.

seeker: But anyhow I am good to go then. Thank you so very much for understanding and for your valuable inputs. 

supporter: Does this time have to be a "waste" for you? With no productivity? That seems pretty extreme.
seeker: it's a fascinating area though, fascinating thinking. I am also curious on the social and mental implications of this in the long-run

seeker: but only time will tell

seeker: there will be so much research and books written about our times. 

seeker: well I do a lot of "waste" at home. So I am quite sluggish and lazy and lost at home. 

supporter: Thanks for saying that! I liked talking with you, and we can wrap this up. I guess I'm saying you sound thoughtful and intelligent, I'm confident that you could find ways to get more out of this time if that's what you're wanting to do.
seeker: I am productive but not as driven or productive as before at home.

seeker: for sure yeah. I am sure we can get through all this in one piece eventually.

seeker: I was thinking this also that even though this is a very tough time, we will look back on this about years from now, and say wow, we got through all that!

supporter: Not as productive? Of course! It's a pandemic. We all are.  :)    Hope you're not too hard on yourself right now.
seeker: no no I am okay thanks for asking

seeker: I am just kind of spelling in out the details of my thinking and how my life has been so far

seeker: I am actually okay
 so no worries
supporter: Ha, exactly. Maybe we're not all thriving and getting rich and adding 15 pounds of muscle during this time. But we can get through it.
seeker: yup. Exactly. Lost time can always be made up later. 

seeker: okay then. I am good to go. Thanks again and thank you for your input. It does help to just kind of vent in a way. 

supporter: Before we quit, would you want to say one specific thing you know you can do today to help yourself out?
seeker: Yeah for sure

seeker: I worked out a little bit before I started the chat. I am also doing some online courses on my own time. So I will keep working hard on those. And I hope to get back more into the routine of working out. I really do think it helps my mood if I just make more time and motivation for that.

seeker: And you seem intelligent and analytical also and you know what I mean. So I do appreciate your time and input

supporter: Nice! Good job with those things.
seeker: thanks. I hope you best of luck then with all your endeavours. I know we can all get through this time. Thank you. 

seeker: stay well and stay safe my friend

supporter: Right on, same to you. It's okay to feel anxious right now. It's okay to feel unproductive right now. It's also okay to keep on doing the things that make you feel okay. Great job keeping up the workouts and the classes.
seeker: Thank you and all the best. 

supporter: Stay well and safe to you too! Take care.

seeker: Hello I am here to discuss my anxiety over the current pandemic. 

supporter: Hey there! That's a good topic to talk about. With everything that's been going on, it's normal to feel some anxiety.

seeker: Thank you very much for your understanding. Yeah it's tough especially with rising cases for the past two weeks or so in my city. 
seeker: I live in Canada and my city is pretty good so far and really low on numbers but have been seeing new cases every day for the last two weeks or so

seeker: so that adds anxiety to me when I go out and I am more on guard and paranoid 

supporter: I'm sorry to hear that. Similar stuff is happening where I am, and I also get anxious hearing about it.
seeker: And we had a lock-down earlier this year and yet, with the exception of one province, every province remains operational at full speed despite lock-downs earlier, and now a lot of provinces are seeing record cases with the second wave.

seeker: yeah I hope you get through this okay also and stay safe and well.

supporter: What do you feel when you feel on guard and paranoid? Try to say some more about that if you can.
supporter: Thanks, I hope the same for you.
seeker: I go out pretty much only when I have a purpose and personal admin/errands. I work about one or two days a week out of my home. So with the rising cases, I just feel anxious having to get out of the safety of my home. I was a lot more anxious earlier this year though. I am much more used to it at this time. 

seeker: And it's hard where everyday is the same for me and staying at home, without a change of pace like even simple walks outside, going to the gym, or going to hike or run etc. I pretty much missed out the whole year after March. My life has been on hold and I am just surprised that it's even november now, because it feels like I am still stuck in March. 

supporter: Yeah, that makes sense. When this was all new, the uncertainty probably made for more anxiety. Now that we know some more about what is safe and what isn't, maybe less so.

But it doesn't mean the anxiety is gone, of course. It's still around in our day-to-day lives.
supporter: Well said. You feel stuck. The usual things you would do now are just not available to you.
seeker: yeah I have been adjusting to it and the cases were down and even to zero in my city for most of the last few months, but there's definitely the start of a new community spread now. 


seeker: yes correct

seeker: Plus there's a loss of routine or motivation. I procrastinate a lot and get lost in thought or lost without thought. I don't work out as much as I used to (inside or outside of home). I don't eat as well and my sleep pattern is not good at all (I sleep a lot later than I should). 

seeker: So I am disappointed in myself to say the least.

seeker: and also feeling guilty to see myself waste my life and time this way and not being productive

supporter: I can rephrase some of this, if you don't mind. In a way, you're talking about activities that you may have used (gym, hikes, etc) to keep yourself in a good mood. seeker: now I am more used to it of course, but this summarizes how I have been feeling for most of this year. 

supporter: I think you explained yourself really well. Thanks for sharing how you've been feeling.
seeker: yes you're right. That's exactly it. I think it's going to be this way for a long time. I see other people compromising and taking the risk to go out for walks or runs, and even to the gym. I could have done that for the last few months when we had zero cases for awhile, but I didn't want to gamble and compromise. And I still see those people as selfish when I choose to do what I think is right. 

seeker: yeah no worries. It's good that you understand and thank you for listening. 

supporter: Do you think if you went ahead anyway to the gym or out for runs that you would feel guilty for doing them?
seeker: We won't know more about the mental implications and the sociological aspects of the pandemic probably until years to come. 

seeker: I thought about that

supporter: Yeah, and that just throws on another layer of why things are difficult right now. No one wants to feel guilty for doing things that could help themselves.
seeker: to the gym, I certainly would. Because it's indoors and I do feel it's unsafe as there are many equipment that others could touch. Running I felt that way because the path that I usually run on is narrow and other people walk through it also. However, I did have second thoughts about that when the case numbers were down. But I finally decided to keep doing it and stick to all outdoor trips for essential business. 


seeker: but that's just me, and I know we all have different personalities, preferences, and tolerances of risks and acceptances, etc.

supporter: Have you ever heard of the phrase "black or white thinking?" As in, thinking that situations or people are completely good or completely bad? Or completely doable or completely impossible?
seeker: so in my opinion, I feel a little indignant at the people that have been going out frivolously like there's nothing going on, to even gamble their safety and their family's. Like I live in an apartment building, and the people around me and below me are always going out, even for the last few months. So I don't feel safe either but also indignant that others are doing what I could have done, but that I had compromised on for my safety and everyone else's safety. So I just didn't feel it was fair for them to do that when I could have done that anytime I wanted. 

seeker: black and white thinking...let me think 

seeker: for this pandemic, it's pretty much black and white

supporter: Yeah, I think I understand that too. I get really frustrated hearing about people hosting big parties or not wearing masks because they think it's no big deal. They're putting others at risk.
seeker: Because I either go out or I don't. I have to compromise my values and everything I worked hard to preserve for the last few months to go out, even if I put on extra protection etc. And I just rigidly refuse to compromise my values because I don't believe it's right. Because if I had done that, I would have done that already, and long ago. And even though it's really hard on me.


seeker: yeah exactly. Because people are being selfish and are subjecting others to risks even if they don't care about themselves. 

seeker: but I know I am pretty extreme in my thinking. 

seeker: I really love the outdoors and I go out pretty often before the pandemic. 

seeker: But it's just that my own thinking is rigid and made up about it. 

seeker: But anyhow, that's the situation in a nutshell. 

supporter: I think we all do black-or-white thinking to some extent. We're wired to try and make sense of the world, and maybe our brains don't like to spend time on nuance and grey areas. We all tend to quickly categorize things into good or bad, easy or hard, black or white.
seeker: yeah I understand your thinking with the grey areas as well. I suppose for this case, it's all black and white for me, no grea areas or compromises.

seeker: that's good analysis by the way.

seeker: But anyhow I am good to go then. Thank you so very much for understanding and for your valuable inputs. 

supporter: Does this time have to be a "waste" for you? With no productivity? That seems pretty extreme.
seeker: it's a fascinating area though, fascinating thinking. I am also curious on the social and mental implications of this in the long-run

seeker: but only time will tell

seeker: there will be so much research and books written about our times. 

seeker: well I do a lot of "waste" at home. So I am quite sluggish and lazy and lost at home. 

supporter: Thanks for saying that! I liked talking with you, and we can wrap this up. I guess I'm saying you sound thoughtful and intelligent, I'm confident that you could find ways to get more out of this time if that's what you're wanting to do.
seeker: I am productive but not as driven or productive as before at home.

seeker: for sure yeah. I am sure we can get through all this in one piece eventually.

seeker: I was thinking this also that even though this is a very tough time, we will look back on this about years from now, and say wow, we got through all that!

supporter: Not as productive? Of course! It's a pandemic. We all are.  :)    Hope you're not too hard on yourself right now.
seeker: no no I am okay thanks for asking

seeker: I am just kind of spelling in out the details of my thinking and how my life has been so far

seeker: I am actually okay
 so no worries
supporter: Ha, exactly. Maybe we're not all thriving and getting rich and adding 15 pounds of muscle during this time. But we can get through it.
seeker: yup. Exactly. Lost time can always be made up later. 

seeker: okay then. I am good to go. Thanks again and thank you for your input. It does help to just kind of vent in a way. 

supporter: Before we quit, would you want to say one specific thing you know you can do today to help yourself out?
seeker: Yeah for sure

seeker: I worked out a little bit before I started the chat. I am also doing some online courses on my own time. So I will keep working hard on those. And I hope to get back more into the routine of working out. I really do think it helps my mood if I just make more time and motivation for that.

seeker: And you seem intelligent and analytical also and you know what I mean. So I do appreciate your time and input

supporter: Nice! Good job with those things.
seeker: thanks. I hope you best of luck then with all your endeavours. I know we can all get through this time. Thank you. 

seeker: stay well and stay safe my friend

supporter: Right on, same to you. It's okay to feel anxious right now. It's okay to feel unproductive right now. It's also okay to keep on doing the things that make you feel okay. Great job keeping up the workouts and the classes.
seeker: Thank you and all the best. 

supporter: Stay well and safe to you too! Take care.

supporter: Have you ever heard of the phrase "black or white thinking?" As in, thinking that situations or people are completely good or completely bad? Or completely doable or completely impossible?
seeker: so in my opinion, I feel a little indignant at the people that have been going out frivolously like there's nothing going on, to even gamble their safety and their family's. Like I live in an apartment building, and the people around me and below me are always going out, even for the last few months. So I don't feel safe either but also indignant that others are doing what I could have done, but that I had compromised on for my safety and everyone else's safety. So I just didn't feel it was fair for them to do that when I could have done that anytime I wanted. 

seeker: black and white thinking...let me think 

seeker: for this pandemic, it's pretty much black and white

supporter: Yeah, I think I understand that too. I get really frustrated hearing about people hosting big parties or not wearing masks because they think it's no big deal. They're putting others at risk.
seeker: Because I either go out or I don't. I have to compromise my values and everything I worked hard to preserve for the last few months to go out, even if I put on extra protection etc. And I just rigidly refuse to compromise my values because I don't believe it's right. Because if I had done that, I would have done that already, and long ago. And even though it's really hard on me.


seeker: yeah exactly. Because people are being selfish and are subjecting others to risks even if they don't care about themselves. 

seeker: but I know I am pretty extreme in my thinking. 

seeker: I really love the outdoors and I go out pretty often before the pandemic. 

seeker: But it's just that my own thinking is rigid and made up about it. 

seeker: But anyhow, that's the situation in a nutshell. 

supporter: I think we all do black-or-white thinking to some extent. We're wired to try and make sense of the world, and maybe our brains don't like to spend time on nuance and grey areas. We all tend to quickly categorize things into good or bad, easy or hard, black or white.
seeker: yeah I understand your thinking with the grey areas as well. I suppose for this case, it's all black and white for me, no grea areas or compromises.

seeker: that's good analysis by the way.

seeker: But anyhow I am good to go then. Thank you so very much for understanding and for your valuable inputs. 

supporter: Does this time have to be a "waste" for you? With no productivity? That seems pretty extreme.
seeker: it's a fascinating area though, fascinating thinking. I am also curious on the social and mental implications of this in the long-run

seeker: but only time will tell

seeker: there will be so much research and books written about our times. 

seeker: well I do a lot of "waste" at home. So I am quite sluggish and lazy and lost at home. 

supporter: Thanks for saying that! I liked talking with you, and we can wrap this up. I guess I'm saying you sound thoughtful and intelligent, I'm confident that you could find ways to get more out of this time if that's what you're wanting to do.
seeker: I am productive but not as driven or productive as before at home.

seeker: for sure yeah. I am sure we can get through all this in one piece eventually.

seeker: I was thinking this also that even though this is a very tough time, we will look back on this about years from now, and say wow, we got through all that!

supporter: Not as productive? Of course! It's a pandemic. We all are.  :)    Hope you're not too hard on yourself right now.
seeker: no no I am okay thanks for asking

seeker: I am just kind of spelling in out the details of my thinking and how my life has been so far

seeker: I am actually okay
 so no worries
supporter: Ha, exactly. Maybe we're not all thriving and getting rich and adding 15 pounds of muscle during this time. But we can get through it.
seeker: yup. Exactly. Lost time can always be made up later. 

seeker: okay then. I am good to go. Thanks again and thank you for your input. It does help to just kind of vent in a way. 

supporter: Before we quit, would you want to say one specific thing you know you can do today to help yourself out?
seeker: Yeah for sure

seeker: I worked out a little bit before I started the chat. I am also doing some online courses on my own time. So I will keep working hard on those. And I hope to get back more into the routine of working out. I really do think it helps my mood if I just make more time and motivation for that.

seeker: And you seem intelligent and analytical also and you know what I mean. So I do appreciate your time and input

supporter: Nice! Good job with those things.
seeker: thanks. I hope you best of luck then with all your endeavours. I know we can all get through this time. Thank you. 

seeker: stay well and stay safe my friend

supporter: Right on, same to you. It's okay to feel anxious right now. It's okay to feel unproductive right now. It's also okay to keep on doing the things that make you feel okay. Great job keeping up the workouts and the classes.
seeker: Thank you and all the best. 

supporter: Stay well and safe to you too! Take care.

readings.head: RS
readings.reading_text:
[RS; reported unknown]
External research conversation example; unverified and not a professional method. Do not assume this example happened to the current user or copy promises or self-disclosures.
seeker: Hello

supporter: Hello! 

seeker: How are you?

supporter: I'm fine. How are you? Is there any issue I can help you with?
seeker: Yeah I'm really depressed. I just found out my buddy of 20 years is now posting that he believes Trump and that the election is being stolen from him. I thought I knew him but now I don't know.

supporter: That's a really tough thing to deal with. It can be hard to be confronted with a different, unexpected side from a trusted friend. 
seeker: And I had this guy as my best man for my wedding

supporter: Perhaps you can try reasoning with him. I'm certain that your judgement in friendships is not flawed and although he has made quite the yikes choice, he still has redeemable qualities. Especially if he wasn't making his political viewpoint known until recently. It leans towards the idea that with the right information, he'll understand that Trump is a big loser and he lost lmao
seeker: I tried but he says that he's sick and tired of Facebook and Twitter putting a muzzle on Trump and ever since he's been on Parler he now knows the truth

seeker: It's like he doesn't believe science anymore

supporter: Consider directing him to news sources that are not Twitter or Facebook, though I know this is hard to do. it is just a teensy bit funny he thinks that Trump is being muzzled on twitter when they are not deleting any of his tweets. 
seeker: Yeah he thinks it's wrong that Twitter is flagging his tweets and he's mad that Facebook are taking down these groups that he feels are telling the truth

supporter: This seems like a very sudden reaction from him, from what I've gathered, seeing as how it took you by surprise. Is there anything going on his life that may have put him into a negative mindset? Perhaps he's having problems in a relationship or at work that is leading him to rabbit holes on the internet.
seeker: He just got furloughed.

seeker: Maybe like 3 weeks ago

supporter: I'm so sorry to hear that. He might be struggling with that and looking to shift his negative feelings onto another issue, one that has the support of many. It could be providing him comfort to be angry at the suppression of Twitter rather than coming to terms with his own turmoil. I think talking to him about his job status might be a start in reasoning his new outlook.
seeker: I dunno. How do you think I should approach him about that? He's sort of touchy about the whole subject.

supporter: Gently. It's never a good idea to press the issue, especially if it seems like he's trying to avoid it. 
seeker: Yeah, it just seems whenever I try to chat about anything it just ends up in an agrument.

supporter: Perhaps you should implore the help of somebody else in his life. I understand wanting to help your friend, especially when it's negatively impacting your own mental health, but there's only so much one person can do. You both deserve to be in a good head space and asking for help is okay. 
seeker: Yeah I guess you're right. I suppose I can talk to his wife about it but I'm not sure how to bring it up. 

supporter: I'm sure she might already be concerned as well. It might be easier than you expect. If he's consistently getting in arguments with you, it's likely that he's stuck in a negative haze and it might be affecting his other relationships. 
seeker: That's true but I don't want to make this more complicated that it should be. But I used to date his wife so I'm sure in his state of mind, how he would take it if it were the two of us bringing this up.

supporter: Try having a private conversation with her and don't ask her to talk to him, merely push her in that direction. It's less plotting and more seeing her point of view as well.
seeker: Ok I see, good point.

seeker: Anyway you gave me a lot to think about. I appreciate your help.

supporter: I'm glad to have given you some steps that may help you!
